header.portalSubtitle: Statutory Portal under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 (Act No. 1 of 2010)

hero.tickerText: Mandatory Annual Re-verification: Under Section 24 of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, all commercial weighing and measuring instruments must undergo periodic re-verification before certificate expiry. Non-compliance invites prosecution under Section 30.
hero.title: Effortless Instrument Certification. Instant Public Verification.
hero.desc: Getting your weighing and measuring instruments certified under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 is now completely paperless and streamlined. Apply online, track inspection progress in real time, and obtain official Schedule XI digital certificates with seamless statutory compliance.
hero.card1Desc: File instrument details online, get inspected on-site by an authorized officer, and receive digitally signed Schedule XI certificates instantly upon approval.
hero.card1Step1: 1. Online Application: Submit specs & pay Schedule XII statutory fees online.
hero.card1Step2: 2. Scheduled Site Visit: Authorized LMO conducts standard MPE calibration tests.
hero.card1Step3: 3. Instant Digital Certification: Receive an officially verified, cryptographically signed Schedule XI certificate.
hero.card2Desc: Verify the statutory compliance and legal validity of any commercial scale, fuel dispenser, or weighbridge in real time against official central records.
hero.card2Step1: 1. Zero-Login Access: Any consumer or inspector can verify directly from a smartphone.
hero.card2Step2: 2. Tamper-Proof Audit: Validate validity dates, serial numbers, and officer signature.
hero.card2Step3: 3. Immediate Trust: 100% cryptographic certainty backed by central statutory ledger.

aboutElmv.title: About Legal Metrology Division (eLMV)
aboutElmv.subtitle: Statutory Regulatory Authority under Legal Metrology Act, 2009 (Act No. 1 of 2010)
aboutElmv.desc: The Legal Metrology Division under the Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, is India's apex statutory authority establishing and enforcing standards of weights, measures, and weighing and measuring instruments. The eLMV digital platform unifies commercial traders, territorial Legal Metrology Officers (LMO), and accredited GATC test laboratories into a high-trust digital workflow guaranteeing calibration precision, asymmetric PKI digital certification, and public verification.
aboutElmv.pillar1Desc: Unified measurement standards across trade and commerce under Central Rules.
aboutElmv.pillar2Desc: Routine inspection and re-verification under Section 24 with strict SLAs.
aboutElmv.pillar3Desc: Asymmetric ECDSA NIST P-256 cryptographic verification and centralized digital record auditing.
aboutElmv.metric1Desc: Tamper-proof asymmetric NIST P-256 ECDSA signatures
aboutElmv.metric2Desc: Statutory verification TAT tracking and enforcement
aboutElmv.metric3Desc: Instant cryptographic validation for commercial protection

section24.title: Legal Metrology Act, 2009 — Mandatory Provisions
section24.sec24Title: Section 24: Verification and Stamping of Weights or Measures
section24.sec24Text: Every person having any weight or measure in his possession, custody or control in circumstances indicating that such weight or measure is being used, or is intended or likely to be used, in any transaction or for protection, shall, before putting such weight or measure into such use, have such weight or measure verified at such place and during such hours as the Controller may direct.
section24.sec30Title: Section 30: Penalty for Use of Unverified Weights or Measures
section24.sec30Text: Whoever uses any weight or measure which has not been verified or re-verified in accordance with the provisions of this Act shall be punished with fine which shall not be less than two thousand rupees, but which may extend to ten thousand rupees, and for the second or subsequent offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
